We're open-sourcing YOLO26-MLX. A native MLX implementation of the YOLO26 object detection models, built from the ground up for Apple Silicon. No PyTorch runtime. No external GPU infrastructure. Train and run real-time object detection directly on your Mac. In internal benchmarks on M4 Pro, the MLX implementation delivered up to 2.6x faster inference and 1.7x faster training compared to PyTorch with MPS. Accuracy stays within 0.5% of the official YOLO26 results. This has powered object detection inside our products since the YOLOv8 generation. Now it's yours. We've been selected as an industry partner for the US Army 's Project ARIA. The initiative brings together leading AI companies to develop and deliver practical AI solutions for soldiers. Not in years. In months. We're contributing to Team Black, building a "Model Armory" that delivers custom AI capabilities to soldiers at every operational level, from datacenters to the tactical edge. Friends--your brain contains ~86 billion neurons with roughly 10,000 connections per cell (varying greatly per region of the brain), yielding your intelligence with over 800 trillion total connections in your mind. Cooler still is how many different kinds of reasoning you do like informal, formal, inductive, deductive, abstract, intuitive, strategic, slow, fast, mathematical, and creative just to name a few. It is difficult to match the raw power of your mind but we are trying to capture parts of it at webAI to promote true human-machine teaming. Below is some exciting news from our webAI Intelligence Lab (the "wIL") about releasing a family of very small formal reasoning models called “TwIL” that can fit on your phone. All models have limitations but we are encouraged about how these models are benching and fit into the webAI Platform on device. I want to publicly thank David Stout for imagining the wIL, our Board for supporting it, Anurag Daram , Cutter Dalton , and Wynne Williams for their scientific diligence on AI reasoning methods, Marcus Stefanide , his team who found these wIL Engineers, and Hugging Face for the original creation of the SmolLM2 models. We also want to thank so many in the AI Community that have been advancing small AI reasoning models such as Yejin Choi (Stanford), Andrej Karpathy (Tesla/Anthropic), Sebastien Bubeck , Ronen Eldan (Microsoft Research), Yuanzhi Li (Microsoft Research / CMU), Song Han (MIT), Tim Dettmers (Allen Institute for AI), Albert Gu , Tri Dao (CMU / Princeton), Arthur Mensch , Guillaume Lample (Mistral AI), Danqi Chen (Princeton University) and many others.

JUST IN: A 50-foot bronze Prometheus is being erected at SpaceX's Starbase in Texas. Not a rendering. Not a concept. The thing is physically being assembled in the desert right now. Atelier Missor, a French foundry near Paris, is behind it. The statue depicts the Greek Titan who stole fire from the gods and gave it to humanity. Someone chose that myth. At that location. On purpose. The symbolism here is not subtle. What does it mean when a rocket company plants a god of fire in the dirt?

Proud to call myself an Expedian as I recently wrapped up my software summer internship at Expedia Group in Seattle! Here, I worked with the Flight Bookings team on systems that handle millions of bookings every month. Here’s the problem we were solving: When flight bookings start failing, someone has to figure out what broke: which supplier, which airline, which error. That used to mean hours of digging through logs, writing queries by hand, and piecing things together across third-party observability tools. We built a platform that catches those drops automatically, shows what’s driving them, and helps the team investigate and route issues in minutes instead of hours. I primarily worked with developing methods for anomaly detection and failure clustering, and helped integrate a natural-language chatbot so product and non-technical teams can pull insights from the system too! I was especially excited to help build something with real impact: helping Expedia recover millions in booking value and cut operational costs. Along the way, I learned a lot about working with large-scale big data systems/frameworks, building scalable data pipelines, and applying data modeling and statistical analysis in production. Check out my website for more info: https://lnkd.in/gQUZuhT4 Huge thanks to Prashanth Kota , Amir M. , Sophia Liu , Shravan Reddy , Jaya Kari , Harshit Jain and Lori Sun for the support this summer, along with all of the fruitful interns I had the pleasure of working with this Summer (pictured below).

Palantir Technologies blew my mind this summer. In the first four weeks of my internship, I production-deployed optimizations that cut a key service’s cost and memory usage by more than 10x. After I finished my designated project early, my lead entrusted me with a major refactor of a fleetwide service. I got the chance to do more than just execute; I put together information by collaborating with cross-team stakeholders, created my own scope and went through design review, and mobilized two team members for execution. I’m thankful to my incredible team for being role models and pushing me to excellence. And I really enjoyed working towards the mission while getting to build my skills in distributed systems and optimization. But what really blew me away is the level of trust I was allowed to earn by proving myself. At no point did I feel like “just the intern”; I got to deliver real value in production and my own abilities were the only factor dictating my impact. Back to Pittsburgh. Excited for what’s ahead :)
